answer_1.quote: We establish a novel large-scale Chinese-English benchmark, named ANAH 2, that assesses the LLMs' ability to annotate the LLM hallucinations sentence-by-sentence, in the scenario of knowledge-based generative question answering.
answer_1.outputs: Fine-grained hallucination annotations per sentence (reference fragment, hallucination type, correction).

answer_2.quote: We evaluate reference fragments and corrections predicted by generative annotators and employ RougeL and BERTScore to compare the generated text with gold-standard human reference ... also apply n‑gram Precision.

answer_3.quote: We first apply existing retrieval methods... GPT-4 is prompted to identify reference fragments and assess whether hallucinations exist.
criteria: Hallucination type (None, Contradictory, Unverifiable, No Fact)

answer_4.quote: Human annotation is conducted following a similar workflow. Annotators fix the GPT‑4 pre‑annotations. Experienced annotators review the annotations and give feedback.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators follow detailed instructions, task descriptions, precautions, examples, and negative cases to label each sentence with reference, hallucination type, and correction.
